sources.situation: `claude plugin list` or `claude plugin install` blocks on a prompt, a network fetch or a lock held by another running claude. `subprocess.run` waits forever, and so do `nio mods install` and the install skill step that calls it. findings.title: `flow show`, a read command, writes into the worktree

findings.fix: open the index read-only, or return `[]` when `.nio/cache/index.db` is absent. Keep the `.gitignore` write out of `connect` calls that only read.

sources.situation: `memory()` calls `index.connect(root)`, which does `mkdir`, writes `.nio/cache/.gitignore` and creates `index.db`. A click on a row in a worktree that has never been indexed therefore creates files in that worktree. This goes against FR-10's "reading the status writes nothing in the worktree". `usage.so_far` is labelled "Writes nothing", and the pane's `ENV` sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` for the same reason. The write is not atomic either: two clicks at once can race on the `.gitignore` existence check. The code swallows every error from `memory` into `{"error"}`, so an unwritable or read-only worktree shows a memory error rather than the real cause.

sources.situation: CT-2 says "one section's failure never stops the others" and a failing section returns `{"error": ...}`. The juries try catches only ValueError and OSError. A ledger that is valid JSON but lacks `sources`, `round` or `jurors` raises KeyError or TypeError. The timeline try catches only `Broken`, so a history line that is not an object raises AttributeError. Either one escapes `show` as a traceback with exit 1 and empty stdout. The pane then shows the last stderr line and no sections, and a hand-edited or merge-damaged committed ledger hides all five sections.

findings.reason: flow.py:1050-1053 catches only ValueError/OSError, and jury.load (jury.py:101) does no validation. A ledger that is valid JSON but lacks `round`, `sources` or `jurors` raises KeyError in juries() and escapes show(). The tasks, cost and memory blocks use `except Exception`.

findings.title: Timeline draws a stage-changing review as a failed review
quotes: x.kind === 'review'
findings.fix: branch on `x.from === x.to` (or on `reasons` being present), not on `kind`.

sources.situation: `timeline` keeps every line whose `from` differs from `to`. A passed review that advances the stage (kind `review`) is kept. The pane branches on `kind === 'review'`, not on the presence of `reasons`. It therefore draws `review <from> · <at> · -` and loses the `to` stage, role, host and model. Only a failed review (same stage) should take that format.

findings.title: Tasks rows in the drill-down are not drawn per task
quotes: a task `<id> <status> · attempts <attempts> · <title>` under its epic
`${t.id} ${t.status} · attempts ${t.attempts} · ${t.title}`
then the tasks are grouped by epic, each marked done, claimed or failing, with its attempts from `state.json`.
findings.fix: in `sections`, draw each epic's name, then one row per entry of `x.tasks` in the CT-12 form.

sources.situation: an implementing effort with two epics gets `tasks` as `[{"epic": ..., "tasks": [...]}]` (CT-5). `sections` passes each epic object to the task row function, which reads `t.id`, `t.status`, `t.attempts` and `t.title`. Every epic line therefore reads `undefined undefined · attempts undefined · undefined`, the epic name is not drawn, and no task row appears. The pack's tests only check the empty case (`tasks: []`), and AC-10 has no test in the Results.

findings.reason: CT-5 shape is `[{"epic","tasks":[...]}]`, but register.tsx:254 passes each epic object to a row function that reads `t.id`, `t.status`, `t.attempts` and `t.title`. Those fields are undefined on an epic, so no task row is drawn.
findings.note: Fix, with re-check: two fix tasks; the reviewers that found them check the fixes once more.

sources.situation: `mods_dir()` returns `src/nio/mods`, which only exists in a built wheel because `force-include` copies `tools/claude-mods` there. No `src/nio/mods` exists in the checkout, so an editable install (the NIO repo itself and `uv run nio`) passes a non-existent marketplace path to `claude plugin install`, and every mod reports `failed`. CT-8 asked for the fallback and a `ValueError` when neither folder exists. The planned test asserts `mods_dir()` is the checkout's `tools/claude-mods`, but the code can't return that.

findings.reason: src/nio/hooks.py:36-38 returns only `Path(__file__).parent / "mods"`, and no `src/nio/mods` exists in the checkout (Glob found none). contracts.md CT-8 (line 90) and grill.md line 188 require the `tools/claude-mods` fallback, so an editable install passes a missing marketplace path to `claude plugin install`.

sources.situation: `show` calls `load(root, slug)` up to four times (stage, timeline, tasks, cost). Each call re-reads and re-parses `history.jsonl`, and a history that is 200 lines long makes that wasteful against the 5 s target in NFR-1. The three nested try blocks, each with its own `Broken` handling, exist only because of the repeated loads.
